items.stem: Which statement about session cookies versus JWT bearer tokens is accurate?

options.text: Neither is universally more secure; each has different trade-offs and threat exposure
options.rationale: Correct: security depends on how each is stored, transmitted and validated, not the format alone.

options.text: JWTs are always more secure than session cookies
options.rationale: A token in localStorage can be stolen via XSS; format alone does not guarantee security.

options.text: Session cookies cannot be protected against CSRF at all
options.rationale: SameSite and antiforgery tokens mitigate CSRF for cookies.

options.text: Bearer tokens are immune to theft
options.rationale: Bearer tokens can be stolen and replayed if exposed.

items.explanation: Correct: security depends on how each is stored, transmitted and validated, not the format alone.

items.stem: Select TWO measures that reduce the risk of session/token theft in a browser app.

options.text: Store the session token in an httpOnly, Secure cookie
options.rationale: Correct: httpOnly keeps the token out of reach of injected scripts, and Secure limits it to HTTPS.

options.text: Set SameSite on cookies and add antiforgery tokens for state-changing requests
options.rationale: Correct: SameSite plus antiforgery tokens mitigate CSRF.

options.text: Keep a long-lived token in localStorage for convenience
options.rationale: localStorage is readable by any injected script, so XSS can steal the token.

options.text: Disable HTTPS to simplify local testing in production
options.rationale: Disabling HTTPS exposes tokens in transit.

options.text: Embed the token in every URL query string
options.rationale: Tokens in URLs leak via logs, history and referrers.

items.explanation: Correct: httpOnly keeps the token out of reach of injected scripts, and Secure limits it to HTTPS.

items.stem: Which OAuth 2.0 flow is recommended for a browser-based SPA today?

options.rationale: Correct: auth-code with PKCE is the recommended flow for public SPA clients.
The implicit flow is discouraged for new SPAs because it exposes tokens in the URL fragment.
ROPC requires handling raw credentials and is discouraged.

options.text: Client-credentials flow for the end user
options.rationale: Client-credentials is for machine-to-machine, not an end-user SPA login.

items.explanation: Correct: auth-code with PKCE is the recommended flow for public SPA clients.
